meta.title: Partnerships, outreach & archive
meta.intro: Every conversation CityAir has had with a potential partner, recorded with its status, what was asked, what was answered and what happens next. Nothing here is a claim of partnership: statuses are stated as they are, including the ones that are still unanswered.
meta.coverageMethod: هر سند با ۵ معیار سنجیده می‌شود: فراداده ۲۰٪ (تاریخ، ساعت، کانال، فرستنده، گیرنده، موضوع) · متن پیام ۴۰٪ (واژه‌به‌واژه=۱۰۰، ترجمه=۹۵، خصوصی=۶۰، خلاصه=۵۰، ناقص=۳۵) · پیوست‌ها/لینک‌ها ۱۵٪ · وضعیت و قدم بعدی ۱۵٪ · برچسب حریم خصوصی ۱۰٪. درصد هر سند از همین فرمول در می‌آید و مجموع = میانگین اسناد.

milestones.title: International Clean Air Dialogue — Dedeman İstanbul Hotel
milestones.body: Two-day intergovernmental dialogue co-organised by UNECE (Convention on Long-range Transboundary Air Pollution), UNEP, the Climate and Clean Air Coalition (CCAC), the Forum for International Cooperation on Air Pollution and the Government of Türkiye, with support from the EU and the UN Development Account; a side event of the 7th International Day of Clean Air for blue skies. Sessions covered the global pollution landscape, science–policy cooperation, transport, financing for clean air, and — Session 6 — communicating air-quality information to the public: from data to action.
milestones.cityAirRole: Attended as a participant. This is where the AQMx-side contact was made and where the first CityAir prototype pages were demonstrated.

sources.label: CCAC events calendar (venue: Dedeman İstanbul Hotel)

milestones.title: MoveGreen replies — positive interest
milestones.body: Maria Kolesnikova, who coordinates the Air Quality Programme at MoveGreen, replied positively to the GreenHope outreach. She states clearly that methane monitoring is not currently a specific area of MoveGreen's work, but that they have strong experience in independent air-quality monitoring, environmental data, citizen engagement, public communication and advocacy. She identifies the opportunity to build the methane component together with a technical partner, and singles out as particularly relevant: validating Earth-observation and remote-sensing data with ground-based monitoring, identifying environmental risk hotspots, developing an air-quality baseline, and engaging local stakeholders.
milestones.cityAirRole: Reply received. Next action: send the non-confidential one-page concept note and propose an introductory call.

milestones.title: Concept note email sent to MoveGreen (Mr. Muradyl)
milestones.body: Outgoing email introducing GreenHope and the XPRIZE Mission Methane partner-development concept, with the five specific asks that structure the collaboration: validate satellite and thermal alerts with ground sensors; monitor waste-burning, landfill and environmental-risk hotspots; develop a methane / PM2.5 baseline; connect with a waste-management or landfill operator; support responsible media engagement.
milestones.cityAirRole: Sent. Awaiting reply; the right focal point for the methane workstream still needs confirming.

milestones.title: COP31, Antalya Expo Center, Türkiye — green start-up track
milestones.body: The 31st UN Climate Change Conference is hosted by Türkiye (COP President: Murat Kurum) with Australia presiding over negotiations (Chris Bowen); the World Leaders' Summit meets 11–12 November. A green start-up AI model has been registered under the author's name for the COP31 innovation track.

cooperation.headline: Five workstreams that match what MoveGreen already said they can do
cooperation.principle: MoveGreen is the local evidence authority; CityAir is the technical and publishing layer. Neither side claims the other's work, and every number published carries its method and its limits.

workstreams.title: Validate Earth-observation and thermal alerts with ground sensors
workstreams.body: Match NASA FIRMS active-fire and thermal anomalies plus Sentinel-2 imagery against the PM readings of MoveGreen's ground network. Deliver a confusion matrix: how often a satellite alert corresponds to a real ground event, and how often it does not. Publish the false-positive rate instead of hiding it.
workstreams.deliverable: Validation note with method, false-positive rate and limits

workstreams.title: Map waste-burning and landfill environmental-risk hotspots
workstreams.body: Build a hotspot register for Bishkek and the surrounding valley: waste-burning sites, landfill fringes, small industrial clusters. Each entry records how it was detected, how it was checked, and who owns the site. This is the register a city needs before it can act.
workstreams.deliverable: Public hotspot register with provenance for every entry

workstreams.title: Develop the methane and PM₂.₅ baseline
workstreams.body: A defensible baseline separates what is measured from what is modelled. MoveGreen's PM network provides the particulate baseline; methane is handled as a measurement plan with named instruments — never as a satellite-derived number presented as quantification. The output is a baseline statement a reviewer can audit.
workstreams.deliverable: Baseline statement: measured, modelled and unknown, separated

workstreams.title: Connect a waste-management or landfill operator
workstreams.lead: MoveGreen introduces; CityAir negotiates the pilot
workstreams.body: The methane workstream needs one operator willing to share operational records (tonnages, gas wells, flaring, collection routes) for a single site. CityAir prepares the data request in the operator's language: what is needed, why, what they get back, and what stays confidential.
workstreams.deliverable: Signed site-level data agreement and a first dataset

workstreams.title: Responsible public communication and citizen engagement
workstreams.lead: MoveGreen leads — this is their established strength
workstreams.body: Bishkek residents already trust MoveGreen's air-quality messaging. This workstream turns new findings into communication that does not exaggerate: what is known, what is uncertain, what people can do this week. CityAir supplies the trilingual (EN/RU/FA) materials and the Telegram bot for field reports from the public.
workstreams.deliverable: Communication pack + field-reporting channel with a published moderation policy

cityAirAdds: The twelve-domain readiness assessment, run with MoveGreen and the city, producing the first fully evidenced Bishkek record (replacing today's synthetic profile)
Evidence-confidence scoring, so a high score with weak proof is visible as such
Innovation briefs with required data, risks, adaptation notes and monitoring indicators
Public dashboard templates, print exports and a Telegram bot for field reporting
Open publication of the knowledge base and the method, so any reviewer can reproduce the result
moveGreenBrings: A 100+ sensor PM network with a track record in Bishkek and Central Asia
The AQ.kg app and its existing audience
Citizen engagement capacity and the 'School Breathes Easily' programme
Media and advocacy reach, and relationships with government
Convening power through the Central Asian Air Quality Platform
aqmAlignment: CityAir's twelve domains map onto AQMx's guidance areas (monitoring, source attribution, emissions inventory, forecasting, health impact, environmental impact assessment, decision support, public engagement, legal framework) — the assessment should be re-checked domain by domain against the current AQMx wording before any submission.
CityAir's five maturity stages follow the same 'stages of capacity' logic published by AQMx, which makes a CityAir result readable to an AQMx audience.
The waste workstream lands directly on AQMx's sectoral guidance 'Eliminating Open Waste Burning' and the waste-management sector guide — the natural home for the Bishkek case study.

The interactive questionnaire is the closest existing instrument; a Bishkek run could be done with both the AQMx questionnaire and the CityAir assessment and the two results compared openly — a genuine contribution rather than a competing product.
Submission route: the AQMx resource exchange library. What AQMx accepts, indexes or lists is AQMx's decision alone; CityAir has no authority to promise placement.

archive.subject: Concept note: a waste-and-methane pilot with MoveGreen (non-confidential, one page)
archive.body:
DRAFT, READY TO SEND — the non-confidential one-pager that was offered in the message of 7 October 2026.

A waste-and-methane pilot: validating satellite alerts with your ground network

The idea in three sentences. Satellite and thermal alerts (NASA FIRMS, Sentinel-2) already flag burning and hotspots around Bishkek, but nobody has published how often those alerts are actually right. MoveGreen has something almost nobody in the region has: a real ground network and public trust. Pairing the two produces a defensible answer for the city — and a method other cities can copy.

What the pilot produces in 90 days: (1) a validation note — how many satellite alerts matched a real ground event, including the false-positive rate, published rather than hidden; (2) a hotspot register — waste-burning and landfill-risk sites in one district, each entry with how it was detected, how it was checked and who owns the site; (3) a baseline statement — measured, modelled and unknown kept apart, with methane handled as a measurement plan, never as a satellite number presented as quantification.

Division of work. MoveGreen brings the ground network and its data, local knowledge of sites and routes, citizen engagement and public communication, and convening power with the city and the region. CityAir brings the method (satellite screening, validation, confidence scoring), the publishing layer (dashboard, trilingual materials, field-report tool), the twelve-domain readiness assessment run jointly with the city, and open method and open data so others can reproduce it.

What we ask for: one pilot district in Bishkek and one named focal point; historical PM data for that district in whatever granularity is comfortable; one introduction to a waste-management, landfill or university partner; written agreement on what may be published, with MoveGreen holding veto over anything describing its own network; and about two hours a week of one person's time during the pilot.

Data, privacy and publication rules. Your data stays yours; nothing is published or redistributed without written agreement. Anything presented as fact carries its method and its limits, and uncertainty is stated rather than smoothed over. No partnership is announced until there is a published output both sides have seen. If either side wants to stop, the pilot stops and the joint material is withdrawn on request.

Status: a reply from MoveGreen expressed interest in learning more; nothing is agreed, funded or announced.

archive.from: Maria Kolesnikova — Air Quality Programme coordinator, MoveGreen
archive.subject: Re: partnership concept — reply from MoveGreen
archive.body: SUMMARY (paraphrased — the full text is kept in the private project archive). MoveGreen thanks CityAir for the outreach after the International Clean Air Dialogue in Istanbul and says they are very interested in learning more about the concept. They confirm that methane monitoring is not currently a specific area of their work, while describing strong experience in independent air-quality monitoring, environmental data, citizen engagement, public communication and advocacy — and experience working with communities and local stakeholders on environmental risks. They see a good opportunity to build the methane-related component together with a relevant technical partner. The four areas outlined in the outreach — validating Earth-observation and other remote-sensing data with ground-based monitoring, identifying environmental risk hotspots, developing an air-quality baseline, and engaging local stakeholders — are described as particularly relevant to their experience.
archive.status: positive reply — awaiting our concept note and a call
archive.notes: QUOTE POLICY: the full message is stored in the private project archive and is published here only as a summary, to respect the sender's privacy. If MoveGreen gives written permission, the full quotation can be placed here verbatim. SOURCE COMPLETENESS: the copy we hold ends mid-sentence ('… are particularly relevant to our experience. I') — the remainder has not been recovered.

Persian original and the confidence table (which claims are verified / unverified) are in the private archive. COP31 registration is personal and not republished.
